desktop.lua_console.view_text1.title: Lua console help
desktop.lua_console.view_text1.text:
You can try a Lua expression here without creating a file. Type 2+3 and press Enter: the console prints 5. Then try x=10 followed by x*2. Variables and the canvas font last until you close the console.

Up recalls your previous line. Esc cancels unfinished input; at an empty prompt it closes the console. :help opens this page and :quit closes the console.

To draw some text, enter these lines:
screen.clear()
screen.font("compact")
screen.text(10,10,"Hello")
screen.show()

For aligned columns, choose screen.font("mono"). "legacy" uses the older calculator header font. screen.measure("Hello") returns the text's width and height.

To plot from Lua:
plot.clear()
plot.function2d(function(x) return x*x end)
plot.show()

Esc closes the plot or stops sampling. Saved examples are in Programming > Lua scripts. Each console input chunk can contain up to 4095 bytes.

desktop.native_help.view_text1.title: Keyboard shortcuts
desktop.native_help.view_text1.text:
These shortcuts work from the calculator stack:

Ctrl+T  Home
Ctrl+A  Command Catalogue
Ctrl+R  Advanced RPL settings
Ctrl+Y  Number bases
Ctrl+K  Find a command in Help
Ctrl+G  Graphs
Ctrl+W  Math workbench
Ctrl+D  Data
Ctrl+F  Formula forms
Ctrl+N  Notebooks
Ctrl+P  Programming
Ctrl+U  Conversions
Ctrl+S  Save session
Ctrl+L  Load session
Ctrl+Q  Save and return to loader

In ordinary lists, arrows select and Enter/F1 opens. Left/Right changes pages. F5 or Esc goes back. Read the bottom labels for other actions.

On calculator soft menus, Tab selects a row. F1-F5 chooses columns 1-5 and Ctrl+F5 chooses column 6. Esc returns to the previous menu and closes the top-level menu.

Source editors use their own shortcuts: Ctrl+A selects all, Ctrl+R replaces text and Ctrl+G goes to a line. Their full list is under F4 Tools > Help.

desktop.edit_file.view_text1.title: Editor shortcuts
desktop.edit_file.view_text1.text:
F1 saves this file. F2 saves it and then runs it. F4 Tools opens editing tools, and F5 or Esc returns. If you have unsaved changes, you can save, discard them or cancel leaving. A failed save keeps the source available.

Move with the arrows. Only the caret and line/column indicator need to change when you move without editing.

Ctrl+K  mark a selection; arrows extend it
Ctrl+A  select all
Ctrl+C  copy
Ctrl+X  cut
Ctrl+V  paste
Ctrl+Z  undo
Ctrl+Y  redo
Ctrl+F  find
Ctrl+R  replace
Ctrl+G  go to line
Ctrl+U  unindent
Tab  indent
Enter  new line with autoindent

The clipboard holds up to 256 bytes. Undo keeps eight recent grouped edits. Save to SD before power-off; leaving the editor or moving to another tool isn't a disk save.

F4 Tools starts with Language reference, Open example and Insert command. Right moves to the remaining editing tools. Examples open as separate named documents. Close the example to return to your original text, cursor, selection and undo history. Save, Discard and Cancel apply to the example separately. Existing filenames cannot be overwritten by Open example.

Insert command: F4 Tools → Insert command. F4 Find searches names; F1 chooses a template and F1 Insert applies it. Edit its arguments for your program. Insertion replaces selected text and is undoable.

Errors offer Edit at line when a source location is available. RPL runtime errors may instead offer Find when one unique occurrence is found; repeated commands cannot be mapped exactly. Back leaves the cursor where it was. CHIP-8 runtime errors map the stopped PC back to the assembly line.

sprite.help.title: Sprite editor
sprite.help.text:
Move around the 16x16 drawing with the arrows. Space or Enter paints the selected pixel; Backspace makes it transparent. F2 Colour chooses a paint colour or the erase option.

F1 saves a colour .sprite file under /db48x/sprites. F4 Tools > Open sprite reloads one. Save before turning the calculator off.

Colour mode has 256 RGB332 colours and transparency. CHIP-8 mode is a one-bit mask: Space/Enter toggles a bit, and colour only affects the preview. Switching a populated colour drawing to CHIP-8 asks before replacing its colours.

Export CHIP-8 mask writes set bits for opaque pixels and clear bits for transparent ones. It doesn't export colour.

To use a saved colour sprite in Lua:
screen.sprite("DEMO.sprite",40,60)
screen.show()

The image is clipped to the screen and transparent pixels leave what's behind them visible.

form_ui.pico_forms_menu.view_text1.title: Formula form help
form_ui.pico_forms_menu.view_text1.text:
A form saves you from entering the same formula over and over. Try WIDTH*HEIGHT with inputs WIDTH=2 and HEIGHT=3, then choose Calculate. You should get 6.

Give each input a name that appears in the formula. Names start with a letter, can contain digits or underscores, and can be up to 12 characters. Calculator command and constant names aren't allowed. You can have six inputs.

Inputs are evaluated in order, so a later input can refer to an earlier one. Each value can be an expression of up to 63 UTF-8 bytes; the formula can use 159.

You can give inputs units such as V, ohm or m/s. Plain numbers acquire those units; a quantity such as 100_cm is converted to them. Result units request a final conversion. Incompatible dimensions report an error.

Graph an input sweep varies one input. The other definitions stay in place; plot axes show magnitudes in the input/result units. Plot bounds are temporary.

The calculator's angle and precision settings apply. Inputs are local to the form and don't replace your variables. Copying a result is your choice. Save .form files through Files; Ctrl+S saves the calculator session separately.

workbench_ui.pico_workbench_menu.view_te.title: Workbench help
workbench_ui.pico_workbench_menu.view_te.text:
For a first solve, choose radians and enter COS(X)=X in Single equation. Use a guess of 1. The answer should be near X=0.7390851332.

A plain expression means expression=0. A local solve starts from your guess; interval search checks a chosen range. Neither guarantees every root. Bad guesses, domain errors and equations with no solution can fail.

Systems use X,Y or X,Y,Z and one guess per unknown. Try X+Y=3 and X-Y=1: X=2, Y=1. Check the reported residuals before using the result.

Symbolic isolate tries to rearrange one equation exactly. If it can't, it reports that rather than silently doing a numerical solve.

Parameter plots keep their own A,B,C. In the plot's F3 controls, choose Parameters: Up/Down selects, Left/Right adjusts, Enter edits, and Esc returns to tracing. Only Store parameters changes calculator variables.

Copy to stack and Store variables are explicit actions. Save equations and parameter definitions through Saved workbenches; results are temporary and are recalculated.

path_ui.pico_path_menu.view_text1.title: Parametric / polar help
path_ui.pico_path_menu.view_text1.text:
For a circle, select radians and Parametric mode. Enter COS(T) for X(T) and SIN(T) for Y(T). Set the T interval to 0 through 2*PI, then choose Plot path. Equal axis scale in Explore makes the circle look round.

Polar mode needs just r(T). Try 1 with the same interval. Trigonometric functions and polar T follow the calculator's angle mode; negative radii are allowed.

Left/Right traces T. F1 shows T,X,Y values and F2 changes the T interval. F4 switches pan/trace, and +/- zooms. F3 opens tangent, go-to-T and equal-scale controls. Esc returns.

Paths use 300 samples. Undefined points leave gaps, and a coarse sample can miss a narrow feature. Tangents can be unavailable at cusps or stationary points. Cartesian roots and X-bound area analysis don't apply to these loops.

Save paths under /db48x/paths. Loading asks before applying the saved angle mode. Plotting preserves calculator variables and stack; use expressions without side effects.

conversion_ui.unit_conversion_menu.view_.title: Unit conversion help
conversion_ui.unit_conversion_menu.view_.text:
Choose Value, From and To, then Convert. Try 100 centimetres to metres: the answer is 1 metre. F1 copies an answer to the stack when you want it there.

Value can be a fraction or expression, such as 1/3. Choose units from the lists or enter a custom unit using DB48X syntax, such as kg*m/s^2 or km/h. Unit names are case-sensitive.

Units must describe compatible dimensions. You can't convert a length to a mass. Celsius and Fahrenheit here are absolute temperatures; a temperature difference uses a different unit. US liquid gallons and imperial gallons are separate choices.

Calculating an ordinary expression leaves your variables, stack and settings alone. Don't use programs with side effects as conversion inputs.

conversion_ui.currency_options.view_text.title: Time and rate-date help
conversion_ui.currency_options.view_text.text:
Leave Automatic NTP and Latest selected for a normal rate refresh. Return to Currency conversion and choose Refresh: it gets current time, updates the clock and downloads rates over HTTPS.

Rate date chooses which observations to request. A historical date doesn't change the clock. Weekends, holidays or provider coverage can give an earlier observation date; check the answer's date.

If NTP is blocked, choose Manual UTC and enter the actual current UTC date and time. Don't enter local time or the historical rate date. You can select Automatic NTP again later.

Timezone changes the displayed clock. Toronto/Eastern follows daylight saving; custom fixed offsets don't. The timezone is saved separately when SD is available. The clock needs another sync after restart.

These update options apply to the next refresh. Standard NTP isn't authenticated. HTTPS still checks the provider's certificate chain, hostname and validity dates.

conversion_ui.wifi_setup.view_text1.title: Wi-Fi help
conversion_ui.wifi_setup.view_text1.text:
Enter your 2.4 GHz network name and WPA2 personal (AES) password. Names and passwords must match exactly. WPA3-only and enterprise networks aren't supported. Only choose Open network if no password is required.

Save credentials on SD if you'd like the calculator to update time quietly at startup. Currency conversion > Refresh explicitly updates both time and rates. Radio status shows the current connection; F4 Details shows attempts and retry timing.

If a connection fails, move closer and try again. A transient WPA2 handshake failure can succeed on retry. Manual refresh can make three join attempts within its 90-second overall limit; the third can reset the driver once.

Startup sync runs up to four sessions within ten minutes, delaying 30, 120 and 300 seconds after failures. Each session can try joining three times within 35 seconds. It doesn't show errors or download rates. A manual refresh takes priority. Cancelling a refresh, changing the clock manually or changing saved credentials stops automatic sync for this boot.

Saved credentials and backups are readable on SD. Forget removes the copies. A failed rate update keeps your current rates. If memory is short, save other work before closing it.

NTP supplies current UTC before HTTPS. Rate downloads still require valid certificates and the correct provider hostname.

ode_ui.pico_ode_menu.view_text1.title: Differential equation help
ode_ui.pico_ode_menu.view_text1.text:
Enter a slope expression in X,Y, not a full equation. Try X-Y, then set X0=0 and Y0=1. Plot solution / direction field shows the approximate solution and slope arrows. For this example, Y=X-1+2*EXP(-X).

Left/Right traces the solution. F1 opens its table, F4 pans and +/- zooms. F3 controls include tangent, initial condition, field/curve visibility and SVG/CSV export. Esc stops sampling or returns.

This solves first-order real initial-value problems. It uses adaptive RK4 step doubling with local tolerance 1e-7 and a budget of 8192 slope evaluations, plus the direction field. The displayed curve has 300 samples. F2 reports partial solutions and evaluation counts.

Stiffness, domain errors or the work budget can leave gaps; local tolerance isn't a global accuracy guarantee. Trigonometric slopes follow angle mode.

Save equations under /db48x/odes. Calculation works without SD. X/Y are local while evaluating, so your calculator variables and stack are preserved. Use expressions without side effects.

notebook_ui.pico_notebooks_menu.view_tex.title: Notebook help
notebook_ui.pico_notebooks_menu.view_tex.text:
Put 2+3 in cell 1, R1^2 in cell 2 and R2/3 in cell 3. Choose Run all. With exact arithmetic the results are 5, 25 and 25/3.

A notebook holds up to 12 expressions and notes. R1..R12 mean earlier cell results; a future result can't be used yet. Notes are for reading and never execute.

Run through a cell starts at cell 1 and stops at that cell. Errors or Esc stop the run without evaluating later cells. Editing, moving or deleting cells invalidates affected results. Check numbered references after rearranging cells.

Nothing runs just because you edit or load a notebook. Choose a Run action when you're ready. Copy the full result explicitly if you want it on the calculator stack; displayed previews can be shortened.

Files under /db48x/notebooks keep expressions and notes, not live results. Run again after loading. A * marks unsaved changes. Ctrl+S saves the calculator session separately.

Notebook calculations read calculator variables and use its angle/precision settings. Result references remain local. Use expressions without side effects because an explicit rerun evaluates them again.

math.matrix.help.title: Matrix help
math.matrix.help.text:
To try matrix calculations, edit A as a 2x2 grid with rows 1,2 and 3,4. Choose Matrix operations > Determinant: the result is -2. Copy it to the stack with F1 if you want to use it there.

Arrows choose a cell; Enter edits its full expression. Fractions such as 1/3 stay exact. F2 Size replaces the grid after confirmation. Matrices can be up to 6x6, with 31 UTF-8 bytes per cell.

For A+B or A-B, A and B need the same dimensions. For A*B, columns(A) must equal rows(B). A/B means A*inverse(B), so B must be square and invertible. Scalar arithmetic can use exact values such as 1/3. Matrix results offer F3 Use in A for chaining; confirm before replacing unsaved A.

Determinant and inverse need square A. Solve uses an augmented matrix with the right-hand side in the last column, up to five unknowns. Eigenvalues are available for 2x2 matrices. Powers / row reduction includes REF, RREF, rank and system classification; negative powers require an inverse.

A and B save independently as .matrix files under /db48x/matrices. Choose different filenames. Import stack matrix reads level 1 without consuming it; it must fit the editor limits. Viewing results preserves operands, variables and stack.

math.finance.help.title: Finance conventions
math.finance.help.text:
For a simple check, set principal 1200, annual rate 0, periods 12 and frequency 12. Choose end-of-period payments. Loan payment gives 100 per period.

Enter rates as percentages: 5 means 5%, not 0.05. For loans and growth, annual rate is nominal and is divided by periods per year. Number of periods is a count, not years. Payments and compounding share that frequency. Choose beginning or end timing as appropriate.

Loan payment is a positive payment magnitude that leaves zero final balance. Compound growth adds no payments; savings with deposits uses the separate Deposit input. Rate/term solving uses Payment. A computed answer doesn't overwrite those inputs automatically.

Amortization shows remaining balance and principal/interest paid through a chosen payment. It doesn't round every intermediate amount to cents. Fees, taxes and lender-specific day counts aren't included.

For NPV and IRR, CF0 is now and later cash flows are equally spaced. Use negative outflows and positive inflows. The discount and IRR rates are per cash-flow period, not annual. There can be several IRRs; interval searches can miss repeated, close or outside roots. All-zero flows leave the rate indeterminate.

Save up to 17 flows and the finance inputs under /db48x/finance. These inputs are separate from engine TVM variables. Copying an answer is explicit.

math.matrix.register_help.title: Matrix registers
math.matrix.register_help.text:
A named register keeps a matrix in a calculator HOME variable. F3 stores A under a name such as RESULTS. F4 Actions also offers Store B. Storing asks before replacing an existing variable.

Choose a register and press F1 to load it into A or F2 into B. The stored matrix and calculator stack stay unchanged. If the working matrix has unsaved changes, replacement asks first.

Save the calculator session before restart to retain HOME registers. They use ordinary RPL variables, not extra permanent slots. RPL programs can use them by name too.

A matrix must fit the editor's 6x6 and 31-byte-per-cell limits to load into the grid. To name a computed matrix, choose its result's F3 Use in A, then store A as RESULTS.

math.complex.help.title: Complex workbench
math.complex.help.text:
Enter Z in rectangular form as real part 1 and imaginary part 2. Enter W as 3 and 4. Arithmetic > Z+W gives 4+6i. Copy the result explicitly if you want it on the stack.

You can enter each value as rectangular components or polar magnitude/phase. Both prompts must succeed before the value changes. Components can be expressions; exact fractions are kept where supported. Polar magnitudes must be nonnegative.

Operations on Z include rectangular/polar form, magnitude, phase, conjugate and all n-th roots for n=2-16. Zero has no defined phase. Roots retain multiplicity, including repeated zero roots. Division by zero reports an error.

The workbench has its own degree/radian phase unit. Changing it converts stored polar phases so the complex values stay the same. If the converted text won't fit, the old inputs and unit are kept. Calculator settings are restored after calculations.

Files saves Z, W, their forms and phase unit under /db48x/complex. Save before power-off; moving to another tool keeps unsaved work only in volatile memory.

Real/imaginary components accept physical quantities, for example real 3_m and imaginary 400_cm give magnitude 5_m. Bare components inherit the unit found in that complex input. Addition/subtraction require compatible dimensions; multiplication/division combine them and n-th roots take the corresponding root unit. Magnitudes can carry units in polar form; explicit phase quantities use r or degrees. Affine temperatures are unsupported; use kelvin. Existing .complex files remain compatible.

Native phase evaluation and n-th roots use a scoped 16-digit numerical profile. Rectangular arithmetic retains exact inputs where supported, and the calculator precision/settings are restored on exit.

math.geometry.help.title: Interactive geometry
math.geometry.help.text:
Six points define the construction: A/B make one infinite line, C/D another, and E/F make a circle with centre E passing through F.

Open Explore, use arrows to select a point, then press Enter to move it. Arrows move by one percent of the visible window span. Enter lets you type coordinates; Esc returns to tracing. F4 switches pan and +/- zooms. F1 Table selects the actual points.

F2 Measure shows line lengths, circle radius, line direction in degrees, line/line intersection and line AB/circle intersections. Coincident, parallel and degenerate lines are reported separately.

Coordinates must be finite and within +/-1e50. Calculations use relative tolerance 1e-12, so nearly tangent or parallel constructions can be unresolved. The drawn circle uses 96 segments; measurements use the numerical geometry, not those screen segments.

Files saves .geometry constructions under /db48x/geometry. Graph actions export SVG or point/sample CSV. Save before restart; unsaved constructions remain only in memory.

Coordinate units applies one unit to points, distances and the window. Choose m, then enter X=100_cm: it becomes 1 metre. Changing m to cm rescales the complete construction. Assigning or removing units asks before reinterpreting existing magnitudes. Distances and coordinate details identify the selected unit; line-direction angles remain degrees. Current files save units; older geometry files load as dimensionless.

math.lab.vector_help.title: Vector workbench
math.lab.vector_help.text:
Enter A and B, then choose Products / geometry or Arithmetic / scale. Components may be real expressions such as 1/3 or SQRT(2). Arithmetic includes A+B, A-B, k*A, A/k and Unit A. Edit k in Arithmetic / scale. Results use DB48X arithmetic and are copied only with F1 Copy.

Try A=[1,0,0] and B=[0,1,0]. Dot is 0, cross is [0,0,1], and the angle is 90 degrees. In 2D, cross gives the signed Z component. Projection onto a zero B and angles involving a zero vector are undefined.

Plot vectors draws A and B through the origin in the native path view. For 3D inputs, choose XY, XZ or YZ. Trace follows A out/back, then B out/back. This is a coordinate projection.

Files / help saves all five math workbenches together. Inputs stay in memory when you leave; use Save to retain them after restarting.

math.lab.probability_help.title: Probability workbench
math.lab.probability_help.text:
Choose Distribution, enter Parameters, then set the point, interval or percentile. Calculate opens a result; F1 Copy puts it on the calculator stack.

Normal example: mean 0, standard deviation 1, interval -1 to 1. Interval probability is about 0.6826894921. Density at 0 is about 0.3989422804; it is not the probability of exactly zero.

Binomial example: n=10, p=0.5. P(X=5) is 0.24609375. Poisson with mean 3 gives P(X=0) about 0.04978706837. Discrete intervals include both integer endpoints.

Inverse CDF uses 0<p<1 and returns the smallest qualifying integer for discrete outcomes. Binomial supports n up to 2000; Poisson mean is at most 1000. Calculations use bounded double precision. Plot shades the selected interval; discrete PMFs are shown in unit-width steps. Files / help saves all five workbenches.

math.lab.region_help.title: Inequalities
math.lab.region_help.text:
Open a boundary, choose Y above/below f(X), and enter its function. Repeat for up to three boundaries. Plot intersection shades points satisfying every enabled condition.

Try Y>=X^2 and Y<=X+2. The curves meet at X=-1 and X=2; the region lies between them over that range. Disabled boundaries keep their formulas.

Inclusive boundaries are solid; strict > or < boundaries are dashed. Shading is a finite-resolution picture. A blank region can mean no overlap, an unsuitable window, or undefined boundary values. Use the plot window and tracing to investigate.

The native graph controls provide tracing, panning, analysis and export. Boundary analysis operates on the selected curve. Files / help saves formulas and relations together with the other math workbenches.

math.lab.multivariable_help.title: Multivariable calculus
math.lab.multivariable_help.text:
Enter F(X,Y); add G(X,Y) when you need a Jacobian. Calculate provides partial derivatives, gradient, Jacobian, Hessian, a value at the point, and a double integral.

Try F=X^2+Y^2 and G=X*Y. Gradient is [2*X,2*Y]. The Jacobian has rows [2*X,2*Y] and [Y,X]. The Hessian of F is [[2,0],[0,2]]. These symbolic results retain X and Y.

At (1,1), F is 2 and the tangent plane is Z=2*X+2*Y-2. Tangent slopes use centred numerical differences; nearby finite samples are required. Plot F and Plot tangent plane use the native surface renderer.

The double integral over X=0..1, Y=0..1 is 2/3. Integral / surface bounds changes either the integration rectangle or the separate surface window. Nearby slopes must agree for a tangent plane. Numerical integration refines a rectangular Simpson grid within 5603 evaluations. Its refinement difference is an estimate for smooth functions, not a rigorous error bound; failure or cancellation keeps the inputs. Files / help saves the inputs and workbench angle mode.

math.lab.algebra_help.title: Symbolic algebra
math.lab.algebra_help.text:
Enter an expression, then choose Transform expression. Simplify, Expand, Collect / factor supported forms and Partial fractions use upstream DB48X rules.

Try (X+1)^2, then Expand: X^2+2*X+1. Collect gathers matching terms and factors supported patterns. It is not a general-purpose polynomial factorization promise. Partial fractions applies to suitable rational expressions such as 1/(X^2-1); unsupported cases report the engine error.

For substitution, choose a variable and replacement, then Substitute variable. With X=2, (X+1)^2 becomes an exact expression equivalent to 9. This does not store X in your calculator variables.

F1 Copy copies the displayed result. Use result replaces the workbench expression only after confirmation. Long results can be copied to the stack even when they exceed the 159-byte formula limit. Files / help saves all five math workbenches together.

advanced.polynomial_help.title: Guided polynomial solving
advanced.polynomial_help.text:
Enter A and B as highest-power-first real coefficients. For X^2-1, choose degree 2 and enter 1, 0, -1. Roots are -1 and 1. X^2+1 gives complex roots. Repeated entries represent multiplicity.

Calculate stays open after each result. F1 Copy adds the result to the calculator stack. With B=X-1, division of X^2-1 gives quotient X+1 and remainder 0. A and B stay unchanged. Plot A uses the native graph engine.

Degrees are limited to 1–8. Leading coefficients must be nonzero. Exact input fractions are retained where the engine supports them; general roots may be approximate or fail to converge. Esc interrupts engine calculations. Files / help saves inputs for all four advanced workbenches.

advanced.ode_help.title: Systems and second-order equations
advanced.ode_help.text:
Use X as the independent variable. In coupled mode enter Y'=F(X,Y,Z) and Z'=G(X,Y,Z). In second-order mode enter Y''=G(X,Y,Z), where Z means Y'. The solver supplies Y'=Z automatically.

Try Y'=Z, Z'=-Y with initial X=0, Y=1, Z=0 and final X=6.283185307. Y follows COS(X), Z follows -SIN(X). The phase portrait is a circle. Second-order G=-Y gives the same solution.

Plot Y and Z, open the phase portrait, or read the table. Native plots support tracing, zoom and export. The solver uses adaptive RK4 step doubling with relative/absolute scale 1e-7 and at most 8192 RHS evaluations. These are numerical estimates for non-stiff problems; stiff or singular equations can fail. A failed or interrupted solve does not show an incomplete curve as a full solution. Esc cancels; inputs remain. Trigonometric expressions use radians.

advanced.engineering_help.title: RLC circuits and RC filters
advanced.engineering_help.text:
Enter resistance in ohms, inductance in henries, capacitance in farads and frequency in hertz. A 1 microfarad capacitor is 1e-6 F. The circuit model uses ideal components.

Series RLC is R+j*(2*pi*f*L-1/(2*pi*f*C)). Parallel RLC combines admittances; a zero resistor or zero inductor shorts that ideal network.

The RC low-pass output is across the capacitor; the high-pass output is across the resistor. Inductance is not used for RC filters. Try R=1000, C=1e-6 and f=159.1549431 Hz. Both magnitudes are about 0.70710678 (-3.0103 dB); low-pass phase is -45 degrees and high-pass is +45.

Bode plots use X=log10(frequency in Hz). X=3 means 1000 Hz. Choose positive sweep limits in hertz. Native trace, zoom and export are available. Files / help saves the circuit inputs.

advanced.statistics_help.title: Inference from your data
advanced.statistics_help.text:
Enter or import an X,Y table in Data / statistics first. Select column X, column Y, or paired differences X-Y here. At least two observations and nonzero sample variance are needed for mean inference. Nothing changes the table.

For X=1,2,3,4,5, the mean is 3 and sample SD is SQRT(2.5). A 95% Student t interval is approximately 1.03676 to 4.96324. Set null mean to 3: the two-sided t statistic is 0 and p-value is 1.

Mean inference assumes independent observations and a normal population, or an adequate large-sample approximation. Paired mode assumes independent pairs and approximately normal differences. A p-value is not the chance the null hypothesis is true.

Fit normal explicitly sends the sample mean and SD to Probability; it does not establish normality. For proportions enter successes and trials. The Wilson score interval remains bounded at 0 and 1; the two-sided score test is a normal approximation and needs adequate expected successes and failures. Small samples need an exact method. Confidence is entered as a fraction, such as 0.95. Files / help saves settings, not the data table.

science.units_help.title: Units across workbenches
science.units_help.text:
Write physical quantities as value_unit: 10_kohm, 100_nF, 2_m or 30_cm. The common Ohm spelling is accepted in quantity-entry prompts too. In Units and dimensions, try (12_V)/(4_ohm) with target A: the result is 3 A. Try (2_m)+(30_cm) with target cm: the result is 230 cm. Incompatible dimensions report an error. F1 Copy is explicit.

Engineering quantity prompts convert compatible inputs to SI. Vector components may carry compatible units; bare components use the first unit found in that vector. Matrix arithmetic delegates unit operations to DB48X. Advanced matrix algorithms that require dimensionless entries keep their restrictions.

Polynomial units declare X and A/B outputs; coefficients use implied output/X^power units. Numerical roots/evaluation return physical units. ODE units declare X,Y,Z and check derivative dimensions. In a second-order equation, Z must have Y/X dimensions. Normal distributions accept measurement units; probabilities and discrete counts remain dimensionless.

Formula forms already support units for named inputs and results. Data units label numerical CSV magnitudes for applied tools; they do not convert the existing table. Keep declarations with the matching data when loading files. Finance percentages, probabilities and integer operations remain dimensionless. Use kelvin rather than affine temperatures for numerical propagation or differential equations.

science.uncertainty_help.title: Independent measurement uncertainty
science.uncertainty_help.text:
Enter a smooth F(A,B,C), nominal values and independent standard uncertainties. Units can be included in values or declared separately. Bare uncertainties use the corresponding measurement units. Use uncertainty zero for an exact input. Choose compatible output units or let the result infer them.

Try F=A*B, A=2_m with sigma=0.1_m, B=3_m with sigma=0.2_m, C=0 with sigma=0. Result: 6 square metres with standard uncertainty 0.5 square metres. With output cm^2, expect 60000 +/- 5000. Copy gives [nominal, standard uncertainty] with units.

This uses first-order numerical derivatives and independent quadrature, sqrt(sum((dF/dAi*sigma_i)^2)). It does not account for correlations and is not a confidence interval. Large uncertainties or nonlinear behavior can invalidate the approximation. Undefined perturbations and inconsistent nearby slopes, including obvious cusps, are rejected. Trigonometric functions use radians. Affine temperature quantities are rejected; use absolute kelvin.

science.fitting_help.title: Interpolation and nonlinear fitting
science.fitting_help.text:
Enter or import an X,Y table first. Interpolation requires at least two strictly increasing, distinct X values. Linear joins samples; shape-preserving cubic (PCHIP) avoids overshoot in monotone data. Evaluate only inside the sampled range; there is no automatic extrapolation. Plots show source observations as well as interpolation.

The exponential demo creates Y=2*EXP(0.5*X)+1 after confirmation. Use model A*EXP(B*X)+C, guesses near A=1, B=0.2, C=0.3, then Fit. Expect A near 2, B near 0.5, C near 1 and small residuals. View/copy coefficients, compare the fit and residuals, or explicitly adopt the result as new guesses.

Fitting is unweighted local least squares with three adjustable parameters, at least four rows, 100 iterations and at most 8192 model evaluations. All three parameters must be identifiable; singular models report failure. Initial guesses and model domain matter. No global optimum, coefficient uncertainty or confidence band is promised. Data units describe numerical X,Y magnitudes; coefficient units follow the chosen model. Save settings in .science and data separately as CSV.

science.discrete_help.title: Integers and recurrences
science.discrete_help.text:
Enter unsigned decimal integers A,B,M, each at most 1e12. GCD and LCM are exact. A modulo B needs B>0. Modular power computes A^B modulo M without building a huge power, and needs M>0.

Try A=12, B=18: GCD is 6 and LCM is 36. With A=2, B=40 and M=1000000007, modular power is 511620083. Prime factors of 360 are 2,2,2,3,3,5. Factoring is limited to A<=1e9 and can be interrupted. Combinations and permutations require 0<=B<=A<=1000 and use exact upstream arithmetic; large results may exceed the readable preview.

For a recurrence, enter F(N,U)=2*U+1, initial U=1 at N=0 and 6 rows. Expect 1,3,7,15,31,63. Values are numerical real scalars, not exact arbitrary-size sequence terms. At most 128 rows are generated. View, plot or export them; replacing the current table always asks. Cancellation/domain/range failure does not install a partial table.

science.signal_help.title: FFT and filters
science.signal_help.text:
FFT uses exactly 8,16,32,64 or128 finite Y samples in row order. They must represent uniform sampling. Set the sample rate in hertz, or infer it from uniformly spaced increasing X times. Empty X units mean seconds for inference; declared time units are converted to seconds. Uneven times are rejected. No rows are silently discarded.

Create the sine demo: 32 samples at 128 Hz of a 16 Hz sine with peak amplitude 1. Choose rectangular window and mean removal, then Analyze FFT. Expect a peak near 16 Hz of amplitude 1, with frequency spacing 4 Hz. Hann/Hamming reduce leakage but spread a tone across bins.

The one-sided amplitude scale divides by the window sum and doubles interior bins, not DC or Nyquist. It describes peak amplitude, not power spectral density or a calibrated noise level. Phase is wrapped in degrees; bins below 1e-12 of the largest amplitude are omitted. Export gives frequency/amplitude CSV; settings and unit labels are saved separately.

Filters include a centered moving average with truncated, renormalized edge windows and one-pole low/high-pass filters. Low-pass starts at the first input; high-pass is input minus low-pass and starts at zero. Choose an odd average span 3..31 and cutoff below half the sample rate. Filtering snapshots the data; only explicit confirmed replacement changes the table. These are basic offline filters, not anti-aliasing before sampling.

research.overview.title: Advanced studies
research.overview.text:
Open Ctrl+T > Math & graphs > More: complex / applied math > Advanced studies. Choose a calculation area, or Connected study / data to capture observations. All six areas share one study with two tables, equations, a numerical matrix and settings. Save it through Files / help before powering off.

Try the defaults: the implicit equation draws a circle of radius 5; the objective has a minimum at (1,-2); the study matrix [[3,1],[1,3]] has eigenvalues 2 and 4. The default transfer function 1/(s+1) has a step response approaching 1.

F5 or Esc returns one level. Results reach the calculator stack only through Copy. Opening a saved study never runs its equations. These are bounded numerical tools: read each tool's qualifications and use Memory / performance for device measurements.

research.contour_help.title: Implicit graphs and optimization
research.contour_help.text:
Enter X^2+Y^2=25, choose Window and set X,Y from -8 to 8, then Plot. One contour at residual level zero draws the circle. For a field such as X^2+Y^2, set levels 1,4,9 to draw three concentric circles.

The native graph uses arrows to probe X,Y, F1 Copy XY, F2 active level, F3 SVG export and F4 Pan. Enter shows the field and residual at the crosshair. The crosshair does not snap to a curve. +/- zoom.

Sampling uses an 81 by 81 grid, at most 8192 field evaluations and 1536 cached line segments. Undefined cells leave holes; sub-cell features can be missed. Complexity/storage failures are reported instead of accepting a partial plot. Esc interrupts sampling.

For optimization, use (X-1)^2+(Y+2)^2 with bounds -5..5 on both axes and initial (0,0). Find minimum should return (1,-2), F near zero. Search is local, bounded and numerical; rectangular bounds are the only constraints in this release.

research.linear_help.title: Advanced linear algebra
research.linear_help.text:
Edit matrix A in the existing Matrix workbench, then open Advanced studies > Advanced linear algebra > Import current matrix A. Import copies it after confirmation. Inputs are square, real, numerical and dimensionless, up to 6 by 6.

The default [[3,1],[1,3]] has singular values 4,2, condition 2 and inverse [[0.375,-0.125],[-0.125,0.375]]. QR reconstructs A=Q*R. SVD reconstructs A=U*diag(s)*V^T. The symmetric eigensolver returns eigenvectors as columns alongside eigenvalues 2,4; signs can differ.

For least squares, capture N or more observations into table B. Its first N Y values form b. The SVD pseudoinverse gives a minimum-norm solution, residual norm and rank diagnostic. Singular values <= largest*1e-12 are discarded. A large condition number indicates sensitivity. General nonsymmetric eigenvectors and larger matrices are outside this tool. Original exact/unit-bearing matrix arithmetic remains available.

research.calculus_help.title: Limits, series and improper integrals
research.calculus_help.text:
Set F(X)=SIN(X)/X and point 0, then Numerical limit > Both sides. Nearby values should stabilize near 1. F(X)=1/X does not have a finite two-sided limit there and should be unresolved. These are numerical samples, not symbolic proofs.

For Taylor, set F(X)=EXP(X), point 0 and degree 4. Expect coefficients [1,1,0.5,0.1666666667,0.0416666667] for ascending powers of X. Supported symbolic derivatives are evaluated numerically. Unsupported derivatives fail explicitly. Plot shows the local polynomial over X0 +/-1, without a remainder bound.

For a finite sum use F(X)=X^2, first=1,last=3: expect 14. Product gives 36. Bounds are inclusive integers, up to 1000 terms.

For an improper integral use EXP(-X), first=0 and First bound to +infinity: expect approximately 1. Transformed midpoint refinement stops at its budget if no estimate stabilizes. Singularities and oscillations can defeat refinement; a small change is not a rigorous error bound.

research.statistics_help.title: Statistics and correlated uncertainty
research.statistics_help.text:
Additional distributions supplies uniform, exponential, Student t and chi-square (degrees of freedom up to 10000) CDFs, percentiles and plots. Student t with 5 degrees of freedom has CDF(0)=0.5. An exact binomial test with k=0,n=10,p=0.5 gives two-sided p=0.001953125 using probability ordering.

Capture observations into study A before weighted fitting. Choose a line or quadratic and positive relative error scales for the first/last rows; intermediate scales vary linearly. Weights are 1/scale^2. Common variance is estimated from weighted residuals; coefficient intervals use Student t and assume a correct model with independent Gaussian residuals. Welch compares the mean Y values of independent A,B samples with compatible Y units (B is converted to A), allowing unequal variances.

For correlated uncertainty use F=A*B, A=2_m +/-0.1_m, B=3_m +/-0.2_m and C=0 +/-0. Set correlation AB=0.5, AC=BC=0: first-order standard uncertainty should be about 0.608276253 m^2 at nominal 6 m^2. Monte Carlo uses correlated Gaussian measurements and a saved seed. Repeating a seed/settings repeats draws. Its central 95% percentile interval has simulation error and is not a fitted-parameter confidence interval. A draw outside the model domain stops the run.

research.signal_help.title: Signals and control systems
research.signal_help.text:
Study table A starts with a unit-amplitude 16 Hz sine sampled at 128 Hz. Table B starts with a three-sample averaging kernel. Convolution plots the complete discrete sum; correlation plots sum A[i]*B[i+lag]. Combined output length must fit 128 rows. X coordinates are constructed from the declared sample rate, not resampled from irregular observations.

Welch PSD uses 32 or 64 sample Hann segments, mean removal and 50% overlap. A final incomplete Welch segment is omitted; its unused row count is shown before plotting. The one-sided density has units Y^2/Hz. It is not the peak-amplitude FFT introduced in port 24. Longer observations are currently bounded by the 128-row study table.

The default transfer function is H(s)=1/(s+1). Coefficients are highest power first: numerator [1], denominator [1,1]. Pole=-1, no finite zeros. At 1/(2*pi) Hz its gain is about -3.0103 dB and phase -45 degrees. The step response at 5 s is 0.993262053; impulse response is EXP(-t). Bode X is log10(Hz).

Degrees are at most three, numerator degree cannot exceed denominator degree, and time responses require strictly proper functions. Responses compare 1000-step and 2000-step RK4 outputs, rejecting discrepancies above 1e-5 times max(1, output magnitude); fast/stiff or unstable systems can be unresolved. Esc cancels, and inputs remain unchanged.

research.document_help.title: Connected studies
research.document_help.text:
Start in Data / statistics: enter or import observations and declare their units. Open Advanced studies > Connected study / data > Capture current data as A. Confirmation copies observations into the study. Capture a second set as B for two-signal or two-sample work. The original data table remains available.

Equations, matrix values, transfer coefficients, measurements, both tables with their separate X/Y units, settings, title and notes save together in a versioned, checksummed .study under /db48x/studies. Results are transient. Choose Save / open / name / notes, give the study a name and save. Change an input, reopen the saved study, then explicitly choose a calculation to rerun it. Loading never runs formulas.

Sending A or B to Data / statistics asks before replacing observations. Existing session, CSV and workbench formats remain compatible and separate. A failed save retains the previous valid file and unsaved study; backup recovery is supported. Without SD, calculations remain usable. Studies parked in PSRAM are volatile: save before power-off. Loader exit includes an unsaved study in its Save/Leave/Cancel protection.
